answer_1.quote: We introduced the first benchmark for Tunisian Arabic by systematically evaluating LLMs on their ability to generate responses in this dialect. ... To assess the quality of these responses, we conduct both human- and LLM-based evaluations ...
datasets: Dataset of Tunisian Arabic instructions composed of 744 unique instructions collected from crowdsourcing and translating a subset of HuggingFace Helpful Instructions dataset

answer_2.quote: Our analysis reveals that most LLMs struggle with Tunisian Arabic... we prompted ten widely used LLMs... We analyze the agreement and correlation between human and LLM-based rankings... defined GPT-4o as our judge model...
automatic_metrics: LLM-based pairwise comparison using Elo rankings

answer_3.quote: We leveraged LLMs themselves to assess the responses in a self-evaluation framework. Following the LLM-as-a-Judge approach, we prompted the same LLMs to evaluate model responses using the same instruction-response pairs and evaluation criteria.
methods: pairwise evaluation via structured prompts adapted from AlpacaEval benchmark

answer_4.quote: To evaluate model responses, three authors of this paper served as annotators, collectively labeling the 900 evaluation instances.
answer_4.guideline: Response evaluated based on: Quality, Correctness, Relevance and each response individually assessed for Tunisian Arabic Usage on a scale
